title: MCP server manifest (C6)
description: Generated by the starter at build time (target/mcp-manifest.json, the artifact of the reviewed commit) or built at startup from the server's tools/list (CC-140), served at GET /mcp-manifest (requires C2) and registered with PUT /admin/v1/registry/servers/{serverId} (C5). Rules checked in addition to this schema (see README, 'Reguły semantyczne'): serverId == 'mcp-' + system; tool names unique; every resourceRefs[].type and resourceTypes[].parent is declared in resourceTypes; resourceTypes[].type unique, all in one Cedar namespace that equals policies.namespace; each declaration consistent (parent and parentAttribute together, parent in the same namespace, earlyScopeCheck only with a scopePattern, the classification attribute among attributes, idPattern and scopePattern anchored with ^ and $ without a top-level alternation); policies.files names unique; policiesHash recomputed from policies equals the declared one; definition.name == name; definition.inputSchema has no confirmation_code and is closed and bounded (CC-078, CC-123: type object and additionalProperties false at every object level, no open maps, every string with maxLength unless an enum or const, every array with maxItems and items, every number with minimum and maximum, patterns anchored with ^ and $, every node typed, no allOf/anyOf/oneOf/not/if/then/else); definitionHash recomputed from definition and the entry equals the declared one (CC-005).

environment.description: Environment the server was built for (CC-138). Absent means production. A gateway in production mode rejects a manifest with dev (422 manifest_rejected, reason environment_mismatch). Not part of any definitionHash.

internalUrl.description: Informational. The gateway takes serverId -> system/internalUrl only from its own configuration and rejects a manifest that disagrees (C5).

tools.description: Which of the two entry forms applies depends on source: AdapterToolEntry when source is adapter, ToolEntry otherwise (CC-193).

source.description: Absent for a server built on the starter. adapter marks the manifest of an adapter, the sidecar of a foreign MCP server (CC-193): its tool entries carry no risk and no action (an administrator classifies them at approval, outside definitionHash) and no resourceRefs, no resourceTypes and no policies (its policies are its own, outside the platform).

policies.description: The policy fragment of the server (C7), from src/main/resources/mcp/policies/ of its repository: the Cedar schema of its one namespace and its resource policies. Present for a server built on the starter, absent for an adapter. It is validated at registration (base schema plus fragment compose and validate in strict mode, see cedar/entity-builder.md) and is part of what an administrator approves (policiesHash).

namespace.description: The Cedar namespace of the server; every resourceTypes[].type starts with it.

schema.description: Text of schema.cedarschema: exactly one namespace, the server's own.

files.description: The *.cedar files of the server, in file name order.

policiesHash.description: sha256 over the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the policies member (see test-vectors/policies-hash). The gateway recomputes it; a changed hash of a deployed server puts the server in pending_approval until an administrator approves it. Present exactly when policies is.

ResourceTypeDeclaration.description: Everything the entity builder knows about a resource type of this server; there is no built-in type (cedar/entity-builder.md).

attributes.description: Attributes the server's resolver fills from the system (Cedar entity attributes), without the parent attribute and without scopes, which the builder adds.

parent.description: Type of the containing resource, declared in this manifest, same namespace.

parentAttribute.description: Cedar attribute that holds the parent entity; required with parent and only then.

idPattern.description: Anchored regular expression (^...$, no top-level alternation) of the ids of this type: tool arguments, resolved resources. Written in the subset that Java and ECMAScript share; matched against the whole id.

scopePattern.description: Anchored regular expression of the local part of a grantable scope id (<Type>/<local part>). Absent: the type cannot be granted in the scope mapping.

earlyScopeCheck.description: Whether the gateway checks tool arguments of this type against the scopes of the user before the call (context.refs). Only for types whose scope is the exact id; requires scopePattern.

classification.description: The attribute the builder normalizes (trim, ASCII lower case, sets without duplicates); a resource missing a required one is refused (internal_error).

argument.description: Name of a top-level argument of the tool's inputSchema whose value is a resource id (string or array of strings).

ToolEntry.description: Manifest entry of one tool. Every tool that accepts a resource identifier MUST declare resourceRefs (C6).

ToolEntryFields.description: Fields of a manifest tool entry, open for composition (used by the gateway registry API). risk and action are required by ToolEntry and forbidden by AdapterToolEntry.

resourceRefs.description: Always present; an empty array when the tool takes no resource identifier (one canonical form for definitionHash).

definitionHash.description: sha256 over the canonical JSON of definition + risk, action, resourceRefs + system, credential (CC-004, CC-005). Receivers recompute it.

McpToolDefinition.description: Full MCP tool definition as returned by tools/list (CC-005). Input of definitionHash together with risk, action, resourceRefs and the server fields system and credential. title is required (CC-115) and hashed like description (CC-042); icons and _meta are not allowed in v1, because they would reach the client without being pinned.

title.description: Display name shown by MCP clients; required since 3.0.0 (CC-115) and part of definitionHash (CC-042).

inputSchema.description: JSON Schema of the arguments. Must not declare confirmation_code (reserved for the gateway, C11). Closed and bounded (CC-078, CC-123); checked by the semantic rules, because JSON Schema cannot express them for arbitrary nesting.

AdapterToolEntry.description: Manifest entry of a tool of an adapter (CC-193). The adapter does not classify: risk and action are absent (the administrator gives them at approval), resourceRefs is empty (policies are per tool), and definitionHash covers the definition, resourceRefs, system and credential without risk and action.
